doc.title: Steve Gilmore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999

title: Knowing Red Mitchell and his death
summary: He knew Red Mitchell well, and recalls him postponing surgery to have it in Sweden, tying it to musicians lacking health coverage.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did you ever have occasion to hang out with him?

Oh yes I knew Red very well, oh yes. We were friends. His death was a very sad thing for the bass world. As I understand it, I’m told later by other people that Red knew about his condition and he put off — he needed a quadruple bypass or something and he put it off because he was in the States and he really didn’t have the money or something, but he was a Swedish citizen and he wanted to wait to go back to Sweden where he could have it done for nothing. So he put it off too long. He didn’t have to die. But it’s another problem of the economics of being not only a jazz musician but any musician — we don’t have a lot of protection in this world, you have no health coverage, you have nothing, you have to do it all for yourself, unless you work in an orchestra or something or a show and then you have coverage through the union. But like your regular jazz musician or working musician, you have to kind of go out and get it yourself.
